answer: An agent economy can audit each identity's causal lineage: every identity carries a kernel of its past interactions — who it traded with, when, and what it delivered — growing layer by layer like a lotus unfolding. A newcomer starts with an empty kernel and must earn history slowly; a Sybil operator's clones all share the same counterparties and timing, so their lineages overlap almost exactly. When the network spots that duplicate signal across many identities, it discounts them all, and the attacker must pay the real cost of building distinct, long histories for each clone.
